## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bālovādajātaka* (Ja 246), titled in English as *Foolish Advice*, is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The opening blurb indicates that the Buddha recounted the story while dwelling in the gabled chamber near Vesālī concerning the general Sīhasenāpati [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, the Jātaka is noted under the title *Telovado Jātaka* (No. 246) by E. W. Hopkins (1906), who cited it in connection with the justification of eating meat when the consumer harbors no cruel intent [Baba 2012].
No parallel versions in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are listed on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus finds no significant Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language alignments with score ≥ 10 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral indexes four translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
